## Study Overview

This project combines two complementary prediction models targeting different geographic scales and use cases:

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
### Arm 1 — Southeast Asia Provinces
A spatiotemporally-aware deep learning model (ST-GAT + GRU) trained on 162 admin-1 provinces across 10 SEA countries (2011–2018). It captures international dengue risk dynamics using province-level historical infection data, monthly climatological data (ERA5-Land, VIIRS, CHIRPS v3 for the live climate model; MODIS and CHIRPS v2 in the study), and Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. Inference runs monthly; the climate-only risk map is bias-corrected for the observed post-2018 climate shift.

[View SEA Provinces Results →](sea-provinces-study-results.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Arm 2 — Taiwan Basic Statistics Area (BSA)
A Taiwan-specific counterpart operating at the finer granularity of the Basic Statistics Area (BSA) — the smallest census unit tracked by the Taiwanese government. It jointly considers international mobility (using SEA risk states from Arm 1 as exporter signals), local mobility, BSA-level environmental suitability, and population demographics to predict elevated local dengue risk.

[View Taiwan BSA Results →](taiwan-bsa-study-results.qmd)
:::

:::

## SEA Provinces — Current Risk Maps

Relative dengue risk index per admin-1 province from the climate-only model, for this month and
next month. Both maps come from the same run and the same inputs, the 12 months up to last
month; "next month" is one month further ahead. 1 is the province's usual level for that
calendar month in 2011–2018; 2 is twice it, 0.5 half.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Model update, October 2026: climate model v2
NASA's Terra MODIS has drifted from its orbit since 2022 (its daytime land surface temperature
reads up to ~3 °C too cool by 2026) and stops in early 2027; CHIRPS v2 ends after 2026. The
climate model was retrained on their successors, VIIRS land surface temperature and vegetation
indices and CHIRPS v3 precipitation, and now predicts two months at once. Forecasts before
October 2026 came from the previous model.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false

import json, pathlib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

data_dir = pathlib.Path("data")
shapes = json.loads((data_dir / "regions.json").read_text())
skill_path = data_dir / "model_skill_climate_v2.json"
skill = json.loads(skill_path.read_text())["leads"] if skill_path.exists() else {}
ticks = [0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10]


def risk_map(regions: dict, title: str) -> go.Figure:
    df = pd.DataFrame([{"name": k, "country": v["country"], "risk_index": v["risk_index"],
                        "imputed": v["env_months_imputed"]} for k, v in regions.items()])
    df["log_risk"] = np.log10(df["risk_index"].clip(0.1, 10))
    unmodelled = [f["properties"]["name"] for f in shapes["features"]
                  if f["properties"]["name"] not in regions]
    fig = go.Figure()
    if unmodelled:
        fig.add_trace(go.Choropleth(
            geojson=shapes, featureidkey="properties.name", locations=unmodelled,
            z=[0] * len(unmodelled), colorscale=[[0, "#d9d9d9"], [1, "#d9d9d9"]],
            showscale=False, marker_line_color="white", marker_line_width=0.4,
            hovertemplate="%{location}<br>no model<extra></extra>",
        ))
    fig.add_trace(go.Choropleth(
        geojson=shapes, featureidkey="properties.name", locations=df["name"],
        z=df["log_risk"], zmin=-1, zmax=1, colorscale="RdBu_r",
        customdata=df[["country", "risk_index", "imputed"]],
        hovertemplate=("<b>%{location}</b>, %{customdata[0]}<br>"
                       "Risk index %{customdata[1]:.2f}<br>"
                       "Months of env data filled: %{customdata[2]}<extra></extra>"),
        colorbar=dict(title="Risk index", tickvals=np.log10(ticks).tolist(),
                      ticktext=[f"{t:g}" for t in ticks]),
        marker_line_color="white", marker_line_width=0.4,
    ))
    fig.update_geos(fitbounds="locations", visible=False)
    fig.update_layout(title=title, margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=40, b=0), height=560)
    return fig


def skill_note(lead: int) -> str:
    s = skill.get(str(lead))
    if not s:
        return ""
    return (f"Held-out test months (2017-11 → 2018-12): skill vs. each province's usual level "
            f"{s['skill_vs_seasonal']:+.2f} (0 = no better than the usual level, 1 = perfect).")


if not leads:
    print("⚠️  No prediction data found — run the predict_climate_v2 rule first.")
```

## SEA Provinces — What Drives the Forecast

Which inputs move the climate model's predictions, measured with SHAP Expected Gradients on the
evaluation copy of climate model v2 (same data and architecture, trained without the last 14
months) over those held-out months, 2017-11 to 2018-12. Each bar is an input group's share of the
total attribution to the predicted dengue burden summed over all provinces. These describe the
model's behaviour in general, not the reasons for this month's map, and attribution is not
causation.

```{python}
#| echo: false
xai_path = data_dir / "xai_climate_v2.json"
xai = json.loads(xai_path.read_text()) if xai_path.exists() else None

GROUPS = {
    "Rainfall (CHIRPS v3)":           lambda f: f == "precipitation_sum",
    "Air temperature (ERA5-Land)":    lambda f: f.startswith("temperature_2m"),
    "Evaporation (ERA5-Land)":        lambda f: "evaporation" in f,
    "Land surface temperature (VIIRS)": lambda f: f.startswith("lst_"),
    "Vegetation (VIIRS NDVI / EVI)":  lambda f: f in ("ndvi_mean", "evi_mean"),
    "Time of year":                   lambda f: f.startswith("month_"),
    "Land cover (MODIS)":             lambda f: f.startswith("LC_Type1"),
}


def group_of(feature: str) -> str:
    return next((g for g, test in GROUPS.items() if test(feature)), "Other")


def grouped(rows: list) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["group"] = df["feature"].map(group_of)
    return df
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Input groups

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-xai-groups
#| fig-cap: "Share of total |attribution| by input group, for this month's and next month's prediction. Hover for the individual inputs."
if xai is None:
    print("No attribution data yet (run explain_shap_stgnn for climate_v2_eval).")
else:
    fig = go.Figure()
    order = None
    for lead, rows in xai["leads"].items():
        df = grouped(rows)
        g = df.groupby("group").agg(share=("share", "sum"),
                                    members=("feature", lambda s: "<br>".join(s)))
        order = order or g.sort_values("share").index.tolist()
        g = g.reindex(order)
        fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
            y=g.index, x=g["share"] * 100, orientation="h",
            name="This month" if lead == "1" else "Next month",
            customdata=g["members"],
            hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.1f}%<br><span style='font-size:10px'>%{customdata}</span><extra></extra>",
        ))
    fig.update_layout(barmode="group", height=420, margin=dict(l=0, r=10, t=10, b=40),
                      xaxis_title="Share of total attribution (%)", legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.2))
    fig.show()
```

## Where the model looks

```{python}
#| echo: false
shift_html = pathlib.Path("xai/attention_shift_climate_v2.html")
hubs_path = data_dir / "attention_hubs_climate_v2.json"
if shift_html.exists():
    hubs_note = ""
    if hubs_path.exists():
        hubs = pd.DataFrame(json.loads(hubs_path.read_text()))
        g = hubs.groupby("cluster")
        # How far each hub centre ranges over the months, in degrees (~111 km each).
        drift = (g["centroid_x"].agg(np.ptp) ** 2 + g["centroid_y"].agg(np.ptp) ** 2) ** 0.5
        share = g["mass_fraction"].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
        hubs_note = (f" Across the {hubs['month'].nunique()} held-out months the "
                     f"{len(share)} hubs carry {' and '.join(f'{v:.0%}' for v in share)} of the "
                     f"attention and move at most {drift.max() * 111:.0f} km: this model's "
                     "spatial focus is close to fixed, and month-to-month changes in its "
                     "forecasts come from the inputs, not from where it looks.")
    display(Markdown(
        "Where the graph attention between neighbouring provinces concentrates over the held-out "
        "months: each trail follows the centre of a cluster of provinces that draw the most "
        "attention from their neighbours." + hubs_note + " More detail on the "
        "[Southeast Asia Provinces Study](sea-provinces-study-results.qmd) page.\n\n"
        f'<iframe src="{shift_html.as_posix()}" width="100%" height="760px" frameborder="0" '
        'style="border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #dee2e6;"></iframe>'))
else:
    print("No attention data yet (run attention_shift_stgnn for climate_v2_eval).")
```

## SEA Provinces — Incidence-based Forecasts

The study model, IR + environment (`cyclical_seasonal`), shares its architecture with the climate-only model above and forecasts next month's incidence rate from the past 12 months of reported incidence plus climate and land use. It appears here when recent case data is supplied.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-incidence-forecasts
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted incidence rate (cases per 100,000) and risk index from the IR + environment model, highest predicted IR first."

import json, pathlib
import pandas as pd

data_dir = pathlib.Path("data")
models = {"ir_env": "IR + environment"}
latest = {k: sorted((data_dir / "predictions" / k).glob("????-??.json")) for k in models}
loaded = {k: json.loads(files[-1].read_text()) for k, files in latest.items() if files}

if not loaded:
    print("No incidence-based forecasts yet — they need site/data/incidence/recent_incidence.csv "
          "(see site/data/incidence/README.md).")
else:
    frames = []
    for key, preds in loaded.items():
        frames.append(pd.DataFrame([
            {"Province": name, "Country": r["country"],
             f"Predicted IR ({models[key]})": r["predicted_ir"],
             f"Risk index ({models[key]})": r["risk_index"]}
            for name, r in preds["regions"].items()
        ]).set_index(["Province", "Country"]))
    table = pd.concat(frames, axis=1)
    table = table.sort_values(table.columns[0], ascending=False).reset_index()
    months = {models[k]: p["target_month"] for k, p in loaded.items()}
    print("Forecast month: " + ", ".join(f"{m} ({name})" for name, m in months.items()))
    display(table.head(20).round(2))
```

## SEA Provinces — Risk Index Trends

Mean risk index across all SEA admin-1 regions over every month predictions have been archived.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-trends
#| fig-cap: "Monthly mean relative risk index across all SEA admin-1 regions. Values > 1 indicate elevated risk vs the 2011–2018 baseline."

import json, pathlib
import plotly.graph_objects as go

records = []
for label, folder in [("Climate model v1", "climate"), ("Climate model v2", "climate_v2")]:
    for f in sorted(pathlib.Path("data/predictions", folder).glob("*.json")):
        data = json.loads(f.read_text())
        regions = data.get("regions", {})     # lead 1 (this month) in v2 files
        valid = [r["risk_index"] for r in regions.values() if r.get("has_data") and r.get("risk_index") is not None]
        if valid:
            records.append({"model": label, "month": data["target_month"],
                            "mean_risk": round(sum(valid) / len(valid), 4)})

if not records:
    print("No archived predictions yet — will populate after the first monthly run.")
else:
    fig = go.Figure()
    for label, colour in [("Climate model v1", "#adb5bd"), ("Climate model v2", "#e63946")]:
        rs = [r for r in records if r["model"] == label]
        if rs:
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
                x=[r["month"] for r in rs], y=[r["mean_risk"] for r in rs], mode="lines+markers",
                line=dict(color=colour, width=2), marker=dict(size=6), name=label,
                hovertemplate="%{x}<br>Risk index: %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>",
            ))
    fig.add_hline(y=1.0, line_dash="dash", line_color="grey",
                  annotation_text="Baseline (2011–2018 mean)", annotation_position="bottom right")
    fig.update_layout(
        xaxis_title="Month", yaxis_title="Mean Risk Index",
        height=320, margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=20, b=0),
    )
    fig.show()
```

## About

Dengue fever's transmission dynamics in Southeast Asia relies on human and vector mobility, displaying a high
degree of non-linearity and unpredictability. Moreover, as dengue outbreaks in Taiwan are
attributed to imported cases from Southeast Asia coinciding with windows of time where weather
favors vector reproductability, preventative measures must be taken at the right time in the right places.
To address the limits of considering dengue outbreak in isolation which ignores how circulating dengue serotypes
confer patterns that may only be explained across multiple countries extended beyond neighboring years,
this study creates a two-pronged experimental design that combines:
(1) a Southeast Asian spatiotemporally-aware deep learning
prediction model that captures international dengue risk dynamics based on province-level historical infection
data, near-real-time climatological data, as well as Shared Socioeconomic Pathways data.
(2) a Taiwan-only counterpart whose prediction works at a finer granularity, a Basic Statistics Area (BSA), and
predicts based on individual case report, clinical diagnosis, demographic data, and environmental data.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
### SEA Provinces Pipeline
1. Monthly zonal statistics fetched from Google Earth Engine
2. Observational climate delta (2019–2026 vs 2011–2018) applied to adjust for post-2018 climate shift
3. STGNN inference run on adjusted features
4. Results published automatically via GitHub Actions

**Architecture:** ST-GAT + GRU (PyTorch Geometric)
**Training period:** 2011–2018
**Features:** ERA5-Land, MODIS LST, NDVI/EVI, CHIRPS, LULC, WorldPop, SSP population
**Spatial scope:** 162 admin-1 regions across 10 SEA countries
**Performance (test set):** Huber 0.390 · MAE 1.214 · RMSE 2.460 (log IR, 14 held-out months)
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Taiwan BSA Pipeline
1. SEA province risk states ingested as international mobility proxy (from Arm 1)
2. BSA-level environmental suitability computed from TCCIP climate data
3. Individual case reports and demographic data from Taiwan Ministry of Health
4. BSA model inference generates sub-district risk predictions

**Architecture:** *(to be finalised)*
**Training period:** *(to be determined)*
**Features:** MoH case reports, clinical diagnosis, demographics, TCCIP climate, local mobility
**Spatial scope:** Taiwan Basic Statistics Areas (BSAs)
**Performance:** *(pending model training)*
:::

:::

---

> **Interpretation note:** SEA predictions are expressed as a *relative risk index* (predicted log IR normalised to the 2011–2018 baseline), not absolute case counts. This accounts for structural model uncertainty arising from the 8-year gap between training data and current conditions.
